title: yuanchenyang/lean_low_rank_univariate_sos
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem of Legat, Yuan and Parrilo, "Low-Rank Univariate Sum of Squares Has No Spurious Local Minima" (SIAM J. Optim. 33(3), 2023). For a real univariate polynomial p and a pair of polynomials u = (u₁, u₂), consider the quadratically penalized Burer–Monteiro objective f_p(u) = ‖σ(u) - p‖² with σ(u) = u₁² + u₂², the norm coming from any inner product on ℝ[x]. The formalized theorem states that if p is a sum of two squares (which is the case for any nonnegative  univariate polynomial) and u is a second-order critical point of f_p (vanishing gradient and positive semidefinite Hessian, Definition 3.1 of the paper), then σ(u) = p, equivalently f_p(u) = 0; hence every SOCP, and in particular every local minimum, is a global minimum. The development follows the paper's proof: the gcd decomposition u = a·u₀ with u₀ coprime, the observation that σ(u₀) has no real roots, a Bézout-based "hgroup" lemma writing a sum of squares p as g·q + s·σ(u₀) with s a sum of squares when g and σ(u₀) are coprime, the factor-peeling argument that replaces the quadratic factors of a shared with σ(u₀) by X², and the final certificate argument combining the first- and second-order conditions.
